title: Newton's Second Law
description: The relationship between force, mass, and acceleration: F = m x a.

# Newton's Second Law

Newton's second law relates the net force acting on an object to its acceleration.

## Core equation

F = m x a

- **F** is the NET (resultant) force in newtons (N), not just a single force.
- **m** is the object's mass in kilograms (kg).
- **a** is acceleration in m/s^2, in the same direction as the net force.

## Meaning

An object's acceleration is directly proportional to the net force and inversely proportional to its mass: a = F / m. The same force produces a smaller acceleration on a more massive object.

## Commonly confused points

- What causes acceleration is the NET force. If forces are balanced (resultant zero), the object does not accelerate even though many forces act on it.
- Force does not cause velocity, but a CHANGE in velocity (acceleration). An object can move fast with no net force (Newton's first law).
- Mass (kg) differs from weight (the force of gravity, N). Weight = m x g.

## Examples

A net force of 10 N on a 2 kg object produces an acceleration of 5 m/s^2. A net force of 10 N on a 5 kg object produces an acceleration of 2 m/s^2.
